reason: The cited evidence confirms that SFE influences deformation mechanisms in FCC HEAs (E2) and that composition changes SFE (E3), but no passage directly supports the specific claim that Mn lowers SFE in the quinary alloy compared to its subsets, nor provides SFE data for the ternary/quaternary alloys.
premises: Mn lowers the stacking fault energy (SFE) in the quinary Cr-Mn-Fe-Co-Ni alloy relative to its quaternary/ternary subsets
Lower SFE promotes earlier onset of deformation twinning and/or strain-induced phase transformation
Altered deformation modes (twinning/transformation) change strain hardening rate and ductility
SFE differences, not constituent count alone, explain mechanical property variations among these alloys
